DETERMINING THE PARTIES' OBLIGATIONS UNDER THE CONTRACT 
CHAPTERS 
---=-
Defendant answered 
with a cable refusing to re~ognize plaintiffs 
objection and announcing "We have today ready for shipment 50,000 lbs. 
chicken 2½-3 lbs. 25,000 lbs. broilers 1 ½-2 lbs.," these being the goods 
procured for shipment under the ~econd cont~act, and asked immediate 
answer "whether we are to ship this merchandise to you and whether you 
will accept the merchandise." After sev~ral other cable exchanges, 
plaintiff replied on May 29 "Confirm agam that merchandise is to be 
shipped since resold by us if not enough pursuant to contract chickens 
are shipped the missing quantity is to be shipped within ten days stop 
we resold to our customers pursuant to your contract chickens grade A 
you have to deliver us said merchandise we again state that we shall 
make you fully responsible for all resulting costs." Defenddnt argues that 
if plaintiff was sincere in thinking it was entitled to young chickens, 
plaintiff would not have allowed the shipment under the 
icond contract 
to go forward, since the distinction between broilers and chickens drawn 
in defendant's cablegram must have made it clear that tl e larger birds 
would not be broilers. However, plaintiff answers that the cables show 
plaintiff was insisting on delivery of young chickens and that defendant 
shipped old ones at its peril. Defendant's point would be highly relevant 
on another disputed issue-whether 
if liability were established, the 
measure of damages should be the difference in market value of broilers 
and stewing chicken in New York or the larger difference in Europe, but 
I cannot give it weight on the issue of interpretation. 
Defendant points 
out also that plaintiff proceeded to deliver some of the larger birds in 
Europe, describing them as "poulets"; defendant argues that it was only 
when plaintiffs customers complained about this that plaintiff developed 
the idea that "chicken" meant "young chicken." There is little force in this 
in view of plaintiff's immediate and consistent protests. 
When all the evidence is reviewed, it is clear that defendant believed 
it could comply with the contracts by delivering stewin 
chicken in the 
2½-3 lbs. size. Defendant's subjective intent would not b . significant if 
this did not coincide with an objective meaning of "chicken." Here it did 
coincide with one of the dictionary meanings, with the dE finition in the 
Department of Agriculture Regulations to which the cor. tract made at 
least oblique reference, with at least some usage in the trade, with the 
realities of the market, and with what plaintiffs spo esman had said. 
Plaintiff asserts it to be equally plain that plaintiffs 
own subjective 
intent wa~ to obtain broilers and fryers; the only evidence against this is 
the material as to market prices and this may not have been sufficiently 
bro~g~t home. In any event it is unnecessary to determine that issue. For 
plamtiff has the burden of showing that "chicken" was used in the 
narrower rather than in the broader sense, and this it has not sustained. 
This opinion constitutes the Court's findings of fact and conclusions 
oflaw. Judgment shall be entered dismissing the complaint with costs.
